knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The label and SDS set the ventilation, PPE, storage and disposal requirements, so they are read before opening any product.
NSW LeadSmart states that open-flame torches create lead fumes, and open flames can ignite vapours.

SafeWork NSW advises keeping flames and sparks away from areas where dust is generated, which reduces the chance of a dust explosion. The industry-body guide is not an official source and is not used.
Flammable products are stored per the approved storage procedure and the relevant standard, with AS 1940 listed as the standard to check.
Products are used only as the SDS and manufacturer approve. Mixing changes the hazard and the result.

practicalCriteria: Candidate reads the label and SDS for a sample product and states the ventilation, PPE and disposal controls it requires.
Candidate identifies and removes an ignition source from a mock-up work area before the product is opened.
Candidate places used rags in a labelled container and records the disposal route.
Candidate records the product name, batch, SDS checked and ventilation used on the job record.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Product and SDS register for the mock-up job
Ventilation and ignition source check record
stopWorkCriteria: Product opened without reading the SDS
Open flame used to strip a finish
Products mixed to change the result
Ignition source left in the work area with flammable vapour present
